videos.script: Every credential so far had to be kept somewhere. A secret in a file. A certificate on a disk. {{kept}} A managed identity is the one nobody keeps. Azure creates it for a resource, and holds the credential itself. {{managed}} There are two kinds. A system-assigned identity is born with its resource and dies with it. {{system}} A user-assigned identity is a resource of its own. Many resources can share it, and it outlives them all. {{user}} The code never sees a credential. It asks the platform under it for a token, at an address only that machine can reach. {{imds}} Your lab is not on Azure, so nobody answers there. You will see that refusal, in a list. {{chain}} That list is the order a program tries, from environment variables to managed identity to your own sign-in. {{order}} And the first one configured wins, even when it is wrong. That rule explains a classic incident in production. {{end}}
